title: Late Breaking Results: Wiring Reduction for Field-coupled Nanotechnologies
problem: In Field-coupled Nanocomputing, wire segments incur the same area and delay costs as standard gates, unlike conventional CMOS. Existing physical design methods do not adequately address this unique constraint.
motivation: Field-coupled Nanocomputing is a promising green and atomically-scaled post-CMOS technology whose practical viability depends on effective physical design optimization that accounts for the high cost of interconnection.
method: The algorithm takes a finished circuit layout and minimizes wire segments—a critical goal because in field-coupled nanocomputing (a type of nanoscale computing), wires consume as much area and delay as logic gates do, unlike conventional chips. It works by treating wires as expensive resources and actively seeking ways to reduce them. The method runs fast enough to handle massive designs with millions of basic tiles, and produces circuits that are both physically smaller and faster to operate.
key_novelty: An algorithm that minimizes wires in field-coupled nanocomputing by treating them as expensive resources comparable to logic gates—a strategy that works because this technology makes wires costlier than in regular computer chips.
contributions: Novel post-layout optimization algorithm achieving 20.13% average wire segment reduction in FCN layouts
Demonstrates 34.10% average area reduction and 19.84% critical path length improvement through wire optimization
Maintains scalability for large-scale layouts with millions of tiles, outperforming existing post-layout optimization methods
